segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Hello, Picturerep. Can I help you?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, hi. I saw your advertisement about copying pictures to disk and I’d like a bit more information about what you do.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Sure. What would you like to know?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, I’ve got a box full of old family photos that’s been up in the attic for years, some of them must be 50 or 60 years old, and I’d like to get them converted to digital format.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Sure, we can do that for you.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Right. And what about size? The photos are all sorts of sizes – are there any restrictions?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Well the maximum size of photo we can do with our normal services is 30 centimetres. And each picture must be a least 4 centimetres, that’s the minimum we can cope with.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That should be fine. And some of them are in a frame – should I take them out before I send them?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Yes please, we can’t copy them otherwise. And also the photos must all be separate, they mustn’t be stuck into an album.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK, that’s not a problem. So can you give me an idea of how much this will cost? I’ve got about 360 photos I think.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: We charge £195 for 300 to 400 photos for the basic service.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. And does that include the disk?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Yes, one disk – but you can get extra ones for £5 each.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s good. So do I need to pay when I send you the photos?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: No, we won’t need anything until we’ve actually copied the pictures. Then we’ll let you know how much it is, and once we’ve received the payment, we’ll send the parcel off to you.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Is there anything else you’d like to ask about our services?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. I’ve roughly sorted out the photos into groups, according to what they’re about – so can you keep them in those groups when you copy them?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Sure. We’ll save each group in a different folder on the disk and if you like, you can suggest a name for each folder.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: So I could have one called ‘Grandparents’ for instance?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Exactly.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And do you do anything besides scan the photos? Like, can you make any improvements?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Yes, in the standard service each photo is checked, and we can sometimes touch up the colour a bit, or improve the contrast – that can make a big difference.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. And some of the photos are actually quite fragile – they won’t get damaged in the process, will they?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: No, if any look particularly fragile, we’d do them by hand. We do realise how precious these old photos can be.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Sure.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: And another thing is we can make changes to a photo if you want – so if you want to remove an object from a photo, or maybe alter the background, we can do that.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Really? I might be interested in that. I’ll have a look through the photos and see. Oh, and talking of fixing photos – I’ve got a few that aren’t properly in focus. Can you do anything to make that better?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: No, I’m afraid that’s one thing we can’t do.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Any other information I can give you?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Er ... oh, how long will it all take?

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: We aim to get the copying done in ten days.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Fine. Right, well I’ll get the photos packed up in a box and post them off to you.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Right. If you’ve got a strong cardboard box, that’s best. We’ve found that plastic ones sometimes break in the post.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. Right, thanks for your help. Bye.

segments.speaker: EMPLOYEE
segments.en: Bye.
